newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close lower for 7th day running.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close lower for 7th day running.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed lower for the seventh consecutive day as disappointing 1996 earnings and continuing bouts of economic uncertainty conspired to put a damper on equities, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 1.31 percent to end at 14,906.21 on a volume of 1.2 billion pesos, while Bogota's IBB index slipped 0.27 percent to close at 960.38 on a below average volume of 960.97 million pesos.
In Bogota, decliners were led by Banco Industrial Colombiano, which fell 6.94 percent to 3,350 pesos per share, and blue chip Banco Ganadero, down 1.0 percent to 297 pesos.
"The drops were undoubtedly due to poor 1996 results. Overall, the financial sector is expected to do better however," one broker said.

Banco Industrial Colombiano's 1996 earnings dropped 27 percent from 1995 while Ganadero, the country's largest bank in terms of assets, saw earnings increase by a modest 6.0 percent, according to preliminary figures.
Cementos Caribe, another big loser in Bogota, fell 9.6 percent to close at 4,791 pesos per share. Brokers said a recent hold rating on the stock by ING Barings was seen by market players as negative.
Decliners in Medellin included Corporacion Financiera Nacional y Suramericana. An investment arm of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, it fell 4.21 percent to end at 2,299 pesos a share.

Bancoquia, which gained 3.59 percent in Bogota to close at 2,510 pesos per share, fell 6.91 percent in Medellin to end at 2,560. Brewer Bavaria gained 2.79 percent in Bogota to end at 5,300 pesos a share and closed up 2.12 percent in Medellin.
Economic emergency measures declared by the government last week, and the threat of U.S. economic sanctions, are widely seen as capping market gains at least until March.
